quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Is hearing protection recommended?
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection on every ride to protect your ears.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to stay safe. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing so other drivers can see you, even during the day. Reflective materials also help make you more visible.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run at an angle?

options.text: Turn to cross at a 90-degree angle.
Use the shoulder to slow down first.

questions.explanation: Ride straight across the tracks in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you might move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: Where in your lane should you ride when being passed?
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle. This keeps both you and the other driver safe.

questions.question: What type of gloves should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They improve your grip and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system links the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's brakes work.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms support your weight.
Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit upright so you can use your arms to steer and control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors show everything you need to see.
Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot.
Signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, in addition to using your mirrors.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles are entering the road ahead.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely at the sign. Let any traffic or pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you do not know. Slower speeds give you more time to see and avoid hazards when it is dark.

questions.question: If traveling with a load, the load should be:
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible unless you use saddlebags. Putting a load on a sissy bar can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it harder to balance.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Let other drivers share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better and be seen. It keeps you away from wind and other drivers' blind spots. Your position should keep others out of your lane and give you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: You should use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.
The motorcycle starts to shake or wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch at the same time. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions coming up. This sign warns you that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Welcome other road users into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other road users into your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you away from wind and other drivers' blind spots. Your position should keep others out of your lane and give you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: How should you stop a motorcycle in a normal situation?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both brakes together and downshift to slow down safely.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Everyone on a motorcycle must wear a helmet. This includes riders, passengers, and people on motor-driven cycles or motorized bicycles.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Drivers of larger vehicles may misjudge how fast you are going and where you are.

questions.question: When should you check your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before riding. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.
